proposals.before: Under the house of Yu nothing surpassed the Shao; under the Zhou nothing surpassed the Shao in its Zhou form.
proposals.after: Under the house of Yu nothing surpassed the Shao; under the Zhou nothing surpassed the Zhuo.
proposals.reason: Chinese contrasts 《韶》 (Shao) with 《勺》 (Zhuo); the idiomatic wrongly repeats Shao for the Zhou piece.

proposals.before: The Classic of Poetry says, “What suits the people wins Heaven’s pay.”
proposals.after: The Classic of Poetry says, “Fitting for the people, fitting for persons—receive emolument from others.”
proposals.reason: Chinese quotation ends 受祿於人 (from others), not Heaven; the idiomatic invents Heaven’s pay.

proposals.before: It copied Shang Yang’s statutes and Han Fei’s theory, spurned the kings’ Way, made greed a habit, and offered the people no moral pattern.
proposals.after: It took as teacher the laws of Shen and Shang, practiced Han Fei’s doctrines, spurned the kings’ Way, made greed a habit, and offered the people no moral pattern.
proposals.reason: Chinese 申商之法 names both Shen and Shang; the idiomatic drops Shen and reads only Shang Yang.

proposals.before: The historian's praise quotes Liu Xiang: "Dong Zhongshu could have served a true king—yiyin day and Lü Wang would not outshine him; Guan and Yan, mere tools of hegemons, fall short."
proposals.after: The historian's praise quotes Liu Xiang: "Dong Zhongshu could have served a true king—Yi Yin and Lü Wang would not outshine him; Guan and Yan, mere tools of hegemons, fall short."
proposals.reason: Corrupt English 'yiyin day' misrenders 伊; the paired name with Lü Wang is Yi Yin.

proposals.before: The encomium says: Liu Xiang declared: "Dong Zhongshu had the stuff of a king's assistant—even yiyin day and Lü Wang would not surpass him; as for Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, assistants to hegemons, probably do not reach him."
proposals.after: The encomium says: Liu Xiang declared: "Dong Zhongshu had the stuff of a king's assistant—even Yi Yin and Lü Wang would not surpass him; as for Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, assistants to hegemons, probably do not reach him."
proposals.reason: Literal likewise corrupts 伊 as 'yiyin day' instead of Yi Yin.

proposals.before: Liu Xin answered his father: "yiyin day and Lü Wang are the sage's matched pair—a king cannot rise without them.
proposals.after: Liu Xin answered his father: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang are the sage's matched pair—a king cannot rise without them.
proposals.reason: Same corruption of 伊 as 'yiyin day'; should be Yi Yin beside Lü Wang.

proposals.before: Reaching Xiang's son Xin, he thought: "yiyin day and Lü Wang are mates of the sage; the true king does not rise without obtaining them.
proposals.after: Reaching Xiang's son Xin, he thought: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang are mates of the sage; the true king does not rise without obtaining them.
proposals.reason: Literal repeats the 'yiyin day' corruption for 伊.

proposals.before: The Classic of Changes warns, "He who porter's load rides in a carriage invites robbers."
proposals.after: The Classic of Changes warns, "He who bears a porter's load and rides in a carriage invites robbers."
proposals.reason: Ungrammatical 'He who porter's load rides' obscures the Changes quotation about bearing a load while riding.

proposals.before: Gongyi Xiu, as Lu's minister, divorced his wife for weaving at home, yanked the gardener's greens from his bowl, crying, "I already draw a state salary—I will not snatch the craftsman's or the weaver's living."
proposals.after: Gongyi Xiu, as Lu's minister, expelled his wife in anger when he saw weaving at home; eating at his lodging and chewing mallow, he angrily pulled up the mallow, saying, "I already draw a state salary—shall I again seize the gardener's and the weaving woman's profit?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents yanking greens from his bowl; Chinese has him eat mallow then pull the mallow plants up, and asks about seizing gardeners' and weavers' profit.

proposals.before: Xia took Yu’s legacy whole, so the Annals name no tweaks—the Way stayed one.
proposals.after: Xia took the Yu legacy whole, so no subtractions or additions are mentioned—the Way stayed one.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'the Annals' and 'Yu' as a person; Chinese 夏因於虞 notes Xia inherited the Yu (Shun) line without mentioning the Annals.

proposals.before: Before that, lightning struck the Gaozu shrines; Dong drafted an interpretation at home. Zhufu Yan peeked at it, envied him, stole the draft, and sent it up.
proposals.after: Before that, the Gaozu temple in Liaodong and the hall of the Gaoyuan park at Changling suffered disaster; Dong drafted an interpretation at home. Zhufu Yan visited, saw it privately, envied him, stole the draft, and submitted it.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents lightning and collapses two shrine sites; Chinese specifies Liaodong Gaomiao and Changling Gaoyuan hall disasters, without lightning.

decisions.after: Among the music of Yu, nothing surpassed the Shao; among that of Zhou, nothing surpassed the Zhuo.
decisions.reason: The text contrasts the Shao with the Zhou musical work titled Zhuo; the revision also avoids the draft's repetitive phrasing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 莫盛於《韶》，於周莫盛於《勺》

decisions.reason: The local source is corrupt. Both the received Ode and external Hanshu witnesses read 受祿於天, which the following sentence explicitly glosses; the existing sense of Heaven's reward must be retained while the source and English are repaired separately.

decisions.after: It took the laws of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang as its teachers, followed Han Fei's doctrines, spurned the kings' Way, made greed a habit, and offered the realm no moral pattern.
decisions.reason: 申 and 商 are Shen Buhai and Shang Yang. The full names make the paired reference intelligible, and the external source confirms the sentence ends 天下, not the truncated local 下.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 師申商之法，行韓非之說……敎訓於天下也

decisions.after: The encomium says: Liu Xiang wrote, "Dong Zhongshu had the talent to assist a true king. Even Yi Yin and Lü Wang could add nothing to him; Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, ministers to hegemons, likely fell short."
decisions.reason: The revision restores Yi Yin, expands the abbreviated Guan and Yan, and renders 王佐 and 伯者之佐 without the draft's disparaging addition 'mere tools.'

decisions.after: The encomium says: Liu Xiang declared, "Dong Zhongshu had the talent of an assistant to a true king. Even Yi Yin and Lü Wang could add nothing to him; Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, assistants to hegemons, likely did not equal him."
decisions.reason: The literal revision restores Yi Yin and gives the abbreviated names and political roles in full.

decisions.after: But Liu Xiang's son Liu Xin held: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang were companions fit for sages; without men like them, a true king could not rise.
decisions.reason: The revision restores Yi Yin and corrects 至向子歆以為: Liu Xin held a different view from his father; he did not 'answer' him in dialogue.

decisions.after: But Xiang's son Xin held: "Yi Yin and Lü Wang were companions to sages; if a true king did not obtain them, he could not rise.
decisions.reason: The literal revision restores Yi Yin and correctly introduces Liu Xin's contrasting judgment.

decisions.after: The Classic of Changes warns, "One who carries a burden while riding in a carriage brings robbers upon himself."
decisions.reason: 負且乘 contrasts a porter's burden with the status of riding in a carriage; the revision states that contrast naturally and preserves the causal warning.

decisions.after: When Gongyi Xiu served as chancellor of Lu, he returned home and saw his wife weaving silk. Angered, he sent her away. Later, while dining at his residence, he ate mallow greens; in indignation he uprooted the mallow plants, saying, "I already live on a state stipend. Am I also to take the profits of gardeners and women who weave?"
decisions.reason: The draft correctly rejected greens being yanked from a bowl, but this revision makes the sequence and Gongyi Xiu's principle clear while preserving the rhetorical question.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 食於舍而茹葵，慍而拔其葵

decisions.after: Xia inherited from the house of Yu. Only in this case are no additions or subtractions mentioned, because their Way was one and they honored the same things.
decisions.reason: The original invents the Annals. The revision renders 因於虞 as succession from the house of Yu and retains both reasons given for saying nothing about additions or subtractions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 夏因於虞，而獨不言所損益者，其道如一而所上同也

decisions.after: Earlier, the Temple of Gaozu in Liaodong and the hall in Gaozu's funerary park at Changling caught fire. At home, Dong Zhongshu drafted an interpretation of the portent, but before he submitted it, Zhufu Yan called on him, saw the draft in private, and, out of jealousy, stole it and memorialized it to the throne.
decisions.reason: 災 here records fires at two distinct sites, not a lightning strike. The revision identifies both sites and makes the sequence of Zhufu Yan's theft clear.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遼東高廟、長陵高園殿災
